body: if I understand the mirage-kv and irmin-git-mirage correctly, this does not provide us with transactions right now -- but this patch (on top of #25) reduces the number of commits to a minimum (1 per HTTP request) by moving the `batch` operation into the webdav_api. Certainly this is a bit more fragile for potential users of webdav_fs (since destroy and write should be called within a batch only), but I think that overall it is a benefit. See https://github.com/mirage/mirage-kv/issues/29 for discussion about transactions.

author: kahowell
body:
https://issues.redhat.com/browse/ENT-5094

With warning messages rather than verbose error messages with stack traces. Note that this will retry indefinitely...

Note that it was already retrying 10 times by default, but without backoff, and I verified that it failed even with retries a couple
of times in stage environment. By retrying indefinitely (for transient errors only), we'll eventually work past transient issues.
kafka topic lag will detect if we ever get into a situation where this causes issues.

Testing
-------

Run as

```
SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=worker ./gradlew :bootRun
```

Simulate a transient error by replacing the logic in `TallySummaryMessageConsumer#receive` with:

```
throw new ObjectOptimisticLockingFailureException("test", "test");
```

Then use the kafka producer in intellij to queue up a message to `platform.rhsm-subscriptions.tally` with value `{}`.

You can also simulate other errors if desired to see that the retry remains unchanged for other exception types.

author: hmhealey
body:
There's a race condition when switching teams to view an unread channel which has been made more common since we fixed an issue where we actually used to mark the channel as read 3 times when switching teams.

We mark the channel as read on viewing it, but at the same time, we're reloading all of your channels and channel members because you switched team. It's currently possible to mark the channel as read when you change teams and then receive the response to the request so that the channel is marked as read in the UI and then shows as unread. It's not actually unread though.

This is attempting to fix that by checking the last_viewed_at of each channel member before saving those received channel members. If the last_viewed_at is lower in a received channel member, then we've hit this race condition and the result from the server is out of date. In that case, we use the unread status from the existing channel member.

#### Ticket Link
https://mattermost.atlassian.net/browse/MM-44900

#### Release Note
```release-note
Fixed a race condition where switching teams to an unread channel may not appear to mark that channel as read
```

author: lologarithm
body:
Added a checkbox to the raid simulation advanced encounter settings 'Use Health' -- when set it uses the sum of the health of the targets and disables all duration input boxes.

Inside the sim code:

-  `sim.Duration` is set after the pre-sims (estimated duration of the fight) to help out the various tools that need duration (like mana pots).
- `sim.GetRemainingDuration` - now uses avg dps of fight so far to estimate how much time is remaining. We should consider removing this and forcing everyone to use `sim.GetRemainingDurationPercent()`
- Modified all dps metrics to use `sim.CurrentTime` instead of `sim.Duration` for calculating dps
- Added DamageDealt to encouter, this is reset in `sim.reset()` 
- Now in the main sim loop we check either duration (when encounter.EndFightAtHealth ==0) or when encounter.DamageTaken > encounter.EndFightAtHealth
- Hunter melee weave and pets uptime now use `sim.GetRemainingDurationPercent()` instead of doing division on `sim.Duration`
- Warlocks swapping to curse of agony now use the estimated `sim.GetRemainingDuration`. 

Due to the change to DPS being calculated off actual sim.CurrentTime it looks like many dps calculations are changed in small ways. Many tests are now 1-2dps different. I have validated no tests are wildly off.
